reasons: The Genocide Convention entered into force on 1951-01-12, before the interstate application was filed on 1993-03-20.
The dispute concerned alleged conduct in Bosnia and Herzegovina and was adjudicated by the ICJ as a dispute under the Genocide Convention.

Bosnia and Herzegovina recorded succession to the Convention on 1992-12-29, and the ICJ final judgment affirmed jurisdiction over the respondent for the dispute despite later status and reservation arguments.
The dispute concerned interpretation, application or fulfilment of the Genocide Convention and State responsibility claims of the kind addressed by Article IX.
The ICJ expressly affirmed jurisdiction on the basis of Article IX of the Genocide Convention for the dispute filed on 1993-03-20.

reasoning: Applicability here means that the Convention and Article IX supplied an applicable legal and jurisdictional framework for the dispute; it does not predetermine the merits.
Later accession/reservation/objection history is preserved as data and not flattened into a new jurisdiction conclusion contrary to the final ICJ judgment.
